attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Will' is firm. 'I believe will dwarf' is an unqualified belief, not a probability hedge, so it is a scored forecast. All three harms and the dot-com comparison are kept, and no deadline is added.

contract.note: The plain reading needs all three harms. Taking 'tens of thousands' as at least 20,000 is ordinary. Not counting interim continued investment as a contradiction is fair to an undated forecast. The ambiguity flags are listed properly.

evidence.note: Counts of AI-cited layoff announcements by employers. These are announcements, not completed dismissals shown to be caused by the boom or a collapse. Not regional and not a depression measure.
UC account of a study on projected water infrastructure needs of data centers. It covers projected pressure, not realised lasting chaos attributable to generative AI.
Funding stayed concentrated in AI through Q3 2026, so no collapse is evident yet. It does not rule out a future depression and is not a regional measure.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm, undated forecast. The evidence does not establish all three harms (attributable completed layoffs, lasting environmental and infrastructure chaos, a Silicon Valley downturn larger than the dot-com bust), so the early-resolution rule is not met. Continued AI funding cannot contradict an open-horizon forecast. Unresolved.
